EXAMPLES

Real diaries, as Jot.

Public-domain diaries converted to plain-text .jot files: a dated entry for each day, the date as it was written kept beside it. Read one in the workspace, or download it and open it in any text editor.

The Diary of Samuel Pepys

Samuel Pepys · 1660–1669 · 3,401 entries · 21 files

Almost every day from January 1660 to May 1669, kept by a clerk of the Navy Board in London: the Plague, the Great Fire, the navy, music and gossip. Old Style dates, converted to modern ones.

From Project Gutenberg, ebook #4200, converted with jot-convert pg4200.txt --calendar julian --name pepys.

The Diary of a Nobody

George and Weedon Grossmith · 15 months, dated from 1888 · 166 entries · 1 file

A comic novel written as a London clerk’s diary, first serialised in Punch in 1888–89. The diary never says its year, so the conversion starts it in 1888, when it appeared.

From Project Gutenberg, ebook #1026, converted with jot-convert pg1026.txt --year 1888 --name nobody.

The file
  • nobody.jot166 entries · 1888-04-03 to 1889-07-11 · 232 KBReadDownload

My Diaries, 1888–1914

Wilfrid Scawen Blunt · 1888–1914 · 1,780 entries · 29 files

A poet and anti-imperialist’s diaries, quoted inside his own narrative of the years before the First World War. The years come from the chapter titles. Also here: the 1870 Paris diary from the appendix, and the 1921 preface.

From Project Gutenberg, ebook #79491 and ebook #79492, converted with jot-convert pg79491.txt --per year --name blunt; jot-convert pg79492.txt --per year --name blunt.
